prompt: Hinsberg test: a secondary amine gives a sulphonamide which is?
explain: R₂N–SO₂Ph has no N–H, so it is not acidic and stays insoluble in NaOH.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Tests for carboxyl and amino groups
prompt: In the Hinsberg test, a tertiary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride shows?
explain: With no N–H, a 3° amine gives no stable sulphonamide (it just dissolves in acid).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Tests for carboxyl and amino groups
prompt: Aliphatic primary amine + HNO₂ (NaNO₂/HCl) gives which observable change?
explain: Unstable aliphatic diazonium decomposes at once, evolving N₂ with alcohol.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Tests for carboxyl and amino groups
prompt: Secondary amine + nitrous acid gives which product (Liebermann's test)?
explain: 2° amines give yellow oily N-nitrosoamines, which respond to Liebermann's nitroso test.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Tests for carboxyl and amino groups
prompt: Aniline with bromine water gives which observation?
explain: The strongly activating –NH₂ group gives tribromination, a white precipitate.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Mohr's salt is chemically which compound?
explain: Mohr's salt is ferrous ammonium sulphate hexahydrate, a double salt.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Mohr's salt is prepared by mixing FeSO₄·7H₂O and (NH₄)₂SO₄ in which mole ratio?
explain: Formula FeSO₄·(NH₄)₂SO₄·6H₂O has 1 FeSO₄ per 1 (NH₄)₂SO₄, so equimolar.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Why is dilute H₂SO₄ added when preparing Mohr's salt?
options: To prevent hydrolysis of Fe²⁺ salt
To act as a dehydrating agent
explain: Dilute H₂SO₄ suppresses hydrolysis of FeSO₄ (and slows its aerial oxidation).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Why is dilute HNO₃ not used instead of dilute H₂SO₄ in Mohr's salt preparation?
options: It is a weaker acid than H₂SO₄
explain: HNO₃ is an oxidising agent and converts Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Why is Mohr's salt preferred over FeSO₄·7H₂O as a standard in redox titrations?
options: It is a stronger reducing agent
It contains more Fe per gram
It is more resistant to aerial oxidation
explain: The double salt is more stable towards air oxidation, so it is a good primary standard.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Chemical formula of potash alum is
explain: Potash alum = K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O, i.e. KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: In potash alum preparation, aluminium scrap is first dissolved in hot
explain: 2Al + 2KOH + 6H₂O → 2K[Al(OH)₄] + 3H₂↑.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Gas evolved when Al scrap reacts with hot KOH solution in alum preparation:
explain: Al displaces H₂ forming potassium tetrahydroxoaluminate.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Mohr's salt and potash alum are both examples of
explain: Double salts exist only in solid state and dissociate into all constituent ions in water.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: An aqueous solution of potash alum gives which ions?
explain: A double salt loses its identity in solution, giving K⁺, Al³⁺ and SO₄²⁻.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: In alum preparation, dilute H₂SO₄ is added to the K[Al(OH)₄] solution. The white ppt formed first is:
explain: Al(OH)₃ forms first, then dissolves in excess H₂SO₄ to give Al₂(SO₄)₃.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Reagent commonly used to convert aniline into acetanilide in the lab?
explain: Aniline is acetylated by acetic anhydride (or acetyl chloride) via nucleophilic acyl substitution.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Zinc dust is added during acetylation of aniline mainly to:
explain: Zn reduces the coloured oxidation products of aniline, so a colourless product is obtained.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Crude acetanilide is usually recrystallised from:
explain: It dissolves in hot water/ethanol and crystallises on cooling.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Pure acetanilide has a melting point of about:
explain: Acetanilide melts at about 114 °C; 214 °C is for p-nitroacetanilide.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Pure p-nitroacetanilide has a melting point close to:
explain: p-Nitroacetanilide melts at about 214 °C, far above acetanilide at 114 °C.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: p-Nitroacetanilide is prepared by nitrating acetanilide with:
explain: The nitrating mixture generates the electrophile NO₂⁺.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Role of conc. H₂SO₄ in nitration of acetanilide:
options: Acts as the solvent for crystallisation
explain: H₂SO₄ protonates HNO₃, which loses water to form the electrophile NO₂⁺.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: In nitration of acetanilide, the major product is para because the –NHCOCH₃ group:
options: Is o,p-directing and sterically hinders ortho
Forms a salt with H₂SO₄ only
explain: The amide N is o,p-directing, and its bulk hinders the ortho positions, so para dominates.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: The minor o-nitroacetanilide is removed from the para isomer by:
options: Steam distillation of the para isomer
explain: The ortho isomer is more soluble in ethanol (intramolecular H-bonding), so the para isomer crystallises out.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Hydrolysis of p-nitroacetanilide with acid or alkali gives:
explain: The amide is cleaved to the free amine, giving p-nitroaniline (an NH₂ → NHCOCH₃ deprotection).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Activated charcoal is added to the hot acetanilide solution to:
explain: Charcoal adsorbs coloured impurities, which are removed by hot filtration.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Acetyl group lowers the activating power of the N in acetanilide because:
options: N lone pair is delocalised onto C=O
The group is strongly electron-donating by +I
N lone pair is fully donated to the ring
explain: Resonance with C=O makes the lone pair less available to the ring, so acetanilide is less activated than aniline.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Direct nitration of aniline gives much m-nitroaniline because in the acid medium aniline forms:
explain: –NH₃⁺ is strongly deactivating and meta-directing; acetylation avoids this and oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide
prompt: Nitration of acetanilide with the nitrating mixture is carried out at low temperature (about 0–10 °C) to:
options: Avoid dinitration and hydrolysis of amide
explain: Nitration is exothermic; keeping the mixture cold prevents polynitration, oxidation and amide hydrolysis.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: Reagents used to diazotise aniline in the aniline yellow preparation:
explain: NaNO₂ with HCl generates HNO₂ in situ, which converts C₆H₅NH₂ into C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: The chromophore responsible for the colour of aniline yellow is:
explain: The azo group conjugated with two aromatic rings makes it a coloured azo dye.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: Diazonium salt with aniline first gives which yellow intermediate, which then rearranges to aniline yellow?
explain: The N-coupling product C₆H₅–N=N–NH–C₆H₅ rearranges to p-aminoazobenzene.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: The rearrangement of diazoaminobenzene to p-aminoazobenzene is promoted by:
explain: Aniline hydrochloride (acid catalyst) in excess aniline at about 40 °C brings about the rearrangement.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: The reaction of acetone or ethanol with I₂ and NaOH to give CHI₃ is called:
explain: Methyl carbonyl compounds undergo trihalogenation and then cleavage to CHX₃ and a carboxylate.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: In the acetone–iodine–NaOH preparation of iodoform, the other organic product is:
explain: Cleavage of the CI₃–CO bond leaves CH₃COONa.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: The active halogenating/oxidising species formed from I₂ and NaOH in iodoform preparation is:
explain: I₂ + 2OH⁻ → I⁻ + IO⁻ + H₂O; NaOI performs the iodination (and oxidation of ethanol).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: Ethanol gives iodoform with I₂/NaOH. The other organic product is:
explain: Ethanol is oxidised to CH₃CHO, which is tri-iodinated to CI₃CHO and cleaved to CHI₃ and HCOONa.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: Iodoform is purified by recrystallisation from:
explain: Iodoform is insoluble in water but soluble in ethanol, so hot ethanol is used to recrystallise it.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Which is a primary standard for acid-base titration?
explain: Oxalic acid is pure, stable and non-hygroscopic; NaOH, KOH and HCl are not.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Why is NaOH not a primary standard?
options: It is hygroscopic and absorbs CO₂
explain: NaOH absorbs moisture and CO₂, so its exact mass gives no exact moles.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Indicator for titrating oxalic acid against NaOH?
explain: Weak acid + strong base: equivalence pH > 7, which suits phenolphthalein.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Mole ratio H₂C₂O₄ : NaOH at the end point?
explain: Oxalic acid is dibasic, so it needs 2 mol NaOH per mole.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: pH range of methyl orange is about?
explain: Methyl orange changes from red to yellow between pH 3.1 and 4.4.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Methyl orange colour in acidic and basic media respectively?
explain: Methyl orange is red in acid (pH < 3.1) and yellow in base (pH > 4.4).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Na₂CO₃ titrated with HCl, phenolphthalein end point: product?
explain: Phenolphthalein marks only the first stage, CO₃²⁻ + H⁺ → HCO₃⁻.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Moles of HCl per mole Na₂CO₃ at the methyl orange end point?
explain: Methyl orange marks complete neutralisation: CO₃²⁻ → H₂CO₃, using 2 H⁺.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Rule for choosing an indicator for a titration?
options: It must be added in large amount
It must be a strong acid
Its range lies in the steep part of the curve
explain: The indicator range must fall within the vertical pH jump around the equivalence point.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Indicator (HIn) changes colour approximately at?
explain: The colour change is seen when the ratio [In⁻]/[HIn] goes from about 1/10 to 10.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Which apparatus is NOT rinsed with the solution it will hold?
explain: Rinsing the flask would change the moles of the solution taken; burette and pipette are rinsed.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Why only 2–3 drops of indicator are used?
options: Indicator itself consumes acid or base
It changes the molarity of titrant
explain: Indicators are weak acids or bases, so excess adds an error in the end point volume.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acid-base titrations and indicators
prompt: Burette reading for colourless solutions is taken at?
explain: Colourless liquids are read at the lower meniscus; dark ones such as KMnO₄ at the upper.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Why is HCl not used to acidify KMnO₄ titrations?
options: It forms a precipitate with Mn²⁺
It decolourises the pink end point
explain: MnO₄⁻ oxidises Cl⁻ to Cl₂, using extra KMnO₄ and giving a wrong (higher) reading.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Why is dilute HNO₃ unsuitable for acidifying a KMnO₄ titration?
options: It is a strong oxidising agent itself
explain: HNO₃ is itself an oxidant and can oxidise the reductant (e.g. Fe²⁺), interfering with the titration.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Oxalic acid is titrated with KMnO₄ at about what temperature?
explain: The reaction is slow in the cold, so the oxalic acid solution is warmed to 60–70 °C.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: In the oxalic acid–KMnO₄ reaction, which species acts as autocatalyst?
explain: Mn²⁺ formed catalyses the reaction, so the first drops decolourise slowly and later ones fast.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Mole ratio KMnO₄ : H₂C₂O₄ in acidic medium is?
explain: Balanced equation: 2 MnO₄⁻ react with 5 C₂O₄²⁻.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Mole ratio KMnO₄ : Fe²⁺ (Mohr's salt) in acidic medium is?
explain: MnO₄⁻ gains 5 e⁻, each Fe²⁺ loses 1 e⁻, so 1 : 5.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Equivalent mass of Mohr's salt (M = 392) in this titration is?
explain: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ involves 1 e⁻ (n = 1), so equivalent mass = molar mass = 392.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Equivalent mass of H₂C₂O₄·2H₂O (M = 126) in KMnO₄ titration?
explain: C₂O₄²⁻ → 2CO₂ loses 2 e⁻ (n = 2), so 126/2 = 63.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Insufficient H₂SO₄ in a KMnO₄ titration gives which brown precipitate?
explain: Without enough H⁺, MnO₄⁻ is reduced only to brown MnO₂ instead of colourless Mn²⁺.

subject: Chemistry
topic: KMnO4 vs oxalic acid / Mohr's salt titration
prompt: Why is KMnO₄ not a primary standard?
options: It contains MnO₂ impurities and decomposes
It is hygroscopic and a gas
explain: It is not obtainable pure (MnO₂ traces) and decomposes in light, so its solution must be standardised.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Cation analysis: group reagents and tests
prompt: Group III-A precipitation uses NH₄Cl along with NH₄OH. What is the role of NH₄Cl?
explain: Common NH₄⁺ suppresses NH₄OH ionisation, so only group III hydroxides (low Ksp) precipitate.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Cation analysis: group reagents and tests
prompt: White precipitate of Pb²⁺ with dil. HCl: PbCl₂ is soluble in?
explain: PbCl₂ is soluble in hot water, unlike AgCl and Hg₂Cl₂; AgCl dissolves in NH₄OH.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Cation analysis: group reagents and tests
prompt: Hg₂Cl₂ turns black on adding NH₄OH due to formation of?
explain: Hg₂Cl₂ + 2NH₃ → Hg + Hg(NH₂)Cl + NH₄Cl; finely divided Hg appears black.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Which species reduces NO₃⁻ to NO in the brown ring test?
explain: FeSO₄ supplies Fe²⁺, which reduces NO₃⁻ to NO; NO then binds Fe²⁺.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Dil. H₂SO₄ on a nitrite salt evolves reddish-brown fumes of?
explain: NO₂⁻ + H⁺ gives HNO₂ which decomposes to NO; NO oxidises in air to brown NO₂.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: White PbSO₄ ppt (from lead acetate test) dissolves in?
explain: PbSO₄ forms soluble complex with hot ammonium acetate/tartrate.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Copper turnings + conc. H₂SO₄ heated with a nitrate salt give which gas?
explain: HNO₃ is liberated and oxidises Cu, itself reduced to reddish-brown NO₂.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Which anion gives no gas with dil. H₂SO₄ but needs conc. H₂SO₄?
explain: CO₃²⁻, S²⁻, NO₂⁻ react with dil. acid; NO₃⁻ requires conc. H₂SO₄.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Sulphide ion gives a yellow ppt with which reagent?
explain: S²⁻ + Cd²⁺ gives yellow CdS.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: AgNO₃ with sulphide ion in the soda extract gives a ppt of which colour?
explain: Ag₂S is black.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Nitrite (not nitrate) gives a brown colour with FeSO₄ in which medium?
explain: Weak acid liberates HNO₂ from nitrite, giving brown [Fe(H₂O)₅NO]²⁺; nitrate does not react.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: Why do Br⁻ and I⁻ not give the chromyl chloride test?
options: They are oxidised to Br₂/I₂ instead
explain: Br⁻ and I⁻ are oxidised to free Br₂ and I₂, so no chromyl halide forms.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: Solid iodide heated with conc. H₂SO₄ evolves which characteristic observation?
explain: HI reduces H₂SO₄ to SO₂ and is itself oxidised to violet I₂ vapour.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: Solid bromide heated with conc. H₂SO₄ gives which visible product?
explain: HBr is oxidised by conc. H₂SO₄ to reddish-brown Br₂, with SO₂ formed.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: Na₂CO₃ extract is acidified with dil. HNO₃ before adding AgNO₃ mainly to…
explain: It decomposes CO₃²⁻, S²⁻, etc., which would also precipitate Ag⁺ salts.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of solution of CuSO4
prompt: On dissolving anhydrous CuSO₄ in water in a calorimeter, the temperature of the solution:
explain: Anhydrous CuSO₄ dissolves exothermically, ΔH_sol ≈ −66 kJ/mol, so the temperature rises.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of solution of CuSO4
prompt: On dissolving CuSO₄·5H₂O crystals in water, the temperature of the solution:
explain: The pentahydrate dissolves endothermically, ΔH_sol ≈ +11 kJ/mol, so the solution cools slightly.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of solution of CuSO4
prompt: In the calorimeter experiment, a temperature rise ΔT gives which sign for ΔH_sol of the salt?
options: Negative, since heat is released to the solution
Sign depends on the salt's mass
explain: Heat gained by the solution and calorimeter is lost by the system, so ΔH = −q/n is negative.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of solution of CuSO4
prompt: To correct for heat exchange with the surroundings, the temperature–time graph is:
options: Read only at the highest point
Extrapolated back to the time of mixing
Read only at the final point
explain: The cooling (or warming) curve is extrapolated back to the mixing time to get the corrected ΔT.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of solution of CuSO4
prompt: A calorimeter open to the atmosphere measures heat q equal to which quantity for the dissolution?
explain: At constant pressure the heat exchanged is q_p = ΔH.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of solution of CuSO4
prompt: In the calorimeter, molar ΔH_sol of CuSO₄ is obtained from heat absorbed by solution by dividing it by:
explain: Molar enthalpy is heat per mole of solute: ΔH_sol = −q/n, where n is the moles of CuSO₄ dissolved.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: The net ionic reaction responsible for ΔH of strong acid–strong base neutralisation is:
explain: Spectator ions cancel; only H⁺ and OH⁻ combine to form water.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: Heat released when 1 mol H₂SO₄ is fully neutralised by excess NaOH (dilute) is about:
explain: 1 mol H₂SO₄ gives 2 mol H₂O, so 2 × (−57.1) ≈ −114.2 kJ.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: Enthalpy of neutralisation is defined per:
explain: It is the heat evolved when 1 gram equivalent of acid is neutralised by a base (1 mol H₂O formed).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: HF neutralised by NaOH releases ≈ −68 kJ/mol, more than −57.1. The reason is:
options: Very high hydration enthalpy of small F⁻
HF is a stronger acid than HCl
HF has a higher molar mass
explain: Exception: the strongly hydrated small F⁻ releases extra heat, so ΔH is more negative than −57.1.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: Weak acid (e.g. CH₃COOH) with strong base gives |ΔH| less than 57.1 kJ because:
options: Energy is absorbed in ionising the weak acid
The base is not fully ionised
explain: Part of the heat evolved is used up in the endothermic ionisation of the weak acid.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: In a calorimeter experiment, heat loss to the surroundings makes the observed |ΔH_neut|:
explain: Lost heat lowers the measured temperature rise, so the observed magnitude is lower than the true value.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: In a thermometric titration of strong acid with strong base, the temperature is maximum at:
explain: Heat evolved is greatest when all H⁺ is neutralised; beyond that, added base only dilutes and cools.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Enthalpy of neutralization: strong acid-base
prompt: Standard ΔH of neutralisation of any strong acid with a strong base in dilute solution is about:
options: −57.1 kJ per mole of acid always
explain: Only H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O occurs, giving ≈ −57.1 kJ (−13.7 kcal) per gram equivalent.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
prompt: In peptization, the sol particles acquire charge by preferential adsorption of which ions?
explain: The peptizing electrolyte supplies an ion common to the precipitate, which is adsorbed and charges the particles.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
prompt: Bredig's arc method combines which two processes?
explain: The arc vaporises the metal (dispersion) and the vapour condenses into colloidal particles in the cold medium.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
prompt: A colloid mill is used to prepare sols by which type of method?
explain: The coarse solid is ground to colloidal size in the dispersion medium, with a stabiliser added.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
prompt: Pouring an alcoholic solution of sulphur into water gives a sulphur sol by which method?
explain: Sulphur is insoluble in water, so it comes out as colloidal particles when the solvent is exchanged.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
prompt: Which of these sols is NOT prepared simply by direct mixing with water?
explain: Gelatin, gum and starch are lyophilic and form on direct mixing. As₂S₃ is lyophobic and needs a special method.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
prompt: Sols formed by direct mixing with the dispersion medium are called reversible because:
options: The residue re-forms the sol on adding medium
explain: Lyophilic sols re-form the sol on remixing with the medium after the dispersion medium is removed.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols
prompt: Which technique removes dissolved electrolytes from a freshly prepared sol?
explain: Dialysis removes ions and small molecules through a semipermeable membrane and purifies the sol.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetics of iodide ion with H2O2
prompt: In the H₂O₂–I⁻ clock reaction, a plot of 1/t (t = time for blue colour) against [I⁻] is expected to be
explain: Rate ∝ 1/t and rate is first order in I⁻, so 1/t ∝ [I⁻], a line through the origin.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetics of iodide ion with H2O2
prompt: Thiosulfate volume is doubled; other concentrations and T are unchanged. The time for blue colour becomes about
explain: Rate is unchanged, but twice as much H₂O₂ must react to consume the thiosulfate, so t doubles.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetics of iodide ion with H2O2
prompt: Rate constants of the H₂O₂–I⁻ reaction are measured at several T. Which plot is linear with slope −Eₐ/R?
explain: The Arrhenius equation gives a straight line for ln k against 1/T with slope −Eₐ/R.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetics of iodide ion with H2O2
prompt: Why does the blue colour appear only after a time lag in this experiment?
options: I₂ is consumed by thiosulfate until it runs out
I⁻ is first converted to IO₃⁻
explain: I₂–thiosulfate reaction is nearly instantaneous, so free I₂ appears only after all thiosulfate is used.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Nitrite interferes in the brown ring test; it is removed before the test by which treatment?
explain: NO₂⁻ reacts with NH₄⁺ to give N₂ (urea also works), so only NO₃⁻ remains for the test.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: A salt with dil. H₂SO₄ evolves a colourless rotten-egg smelling gas. Anion present?
explain: Sulphide with dilute acid releases H₂S, which has a rotten-egg smell.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetics of iodide ion with H2O2
prompt: Rate of H₂O₂ consumption from the thiosulfate clock: t = time for blue colour, [S₂O₃²⁻] = moles/L added.
explain: 1 H₂O₂ gives 1 I₂, which uses 2 S₂O₃²⁻, so Δ[H₂O₂] = [S₂O₃²⁻]/2 over time t.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetics of iodide ion with H2O2
prompt: Overall order of H₂O₂ + 2I⁻ + 2H⁺ → I₂ + 2H₂O with H⁺ in excess, from the experimental rate law?
explain: Order comes from the rate law, not stoichiometry: 1 + 1 = 2, whereas the equation has 5 reactant moles.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Lassaigne's test: N, S, halogens detection
prompt: Violet colour in Lassaigne extract with sodium nitroprusside is due to which species?
explain: S²⁻ attacks the nitroprusside NO group to give the violet complex Na₄[Fe(CN)₅NOS].

subject: Chemistry
topic: Test for alcoholic and phenolic -OH groups
prompt: Alcohol or phenol on adding a small piece of sodium metal evolves which gas?
explain: The acidic –OH hydrogen is replaced by Na, releasing H₂ gas as brisk bubbles.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Test for alcoholic and phenolic -OH groups
prompt: Which –OH compound dissolves in cold aqueous NaOH, helping to distinguish it from a simple alcohol?
explain: Phenol is acidic enough to form soluble sodium phenoxide; simple alcohols are not acidic enough.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Test for alcoholic and phenolic -OH groups
prompt: Benzyl alcohol with Lucas reagent at room temperature gives turbidity:
explain: The benzylic carbocation is resonance-stabilised, so it reacts like a tertiary alcohol.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Test for alcoholic and phenolic -OH groups
prompt: Phenol with benzenediazonium chloride in alkaline medium gives which coloured product?
explain: Azo coupling at the para position of the phenoxide ion gives p-hydroxyazobenzene, an orange-red dye.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Tests for aldehydes and ketones
prompt: Fructose, a ketose, reduces Tollens' reagent because in alkaline medium it:
options: Isomerises to an aldose via an enediol
Is oxidised at its C=O carbon directly
explain: Alkaline medium converts fructose to glucose/mannose through an enediol, and the aldoses reduce Ag⁺.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Tests for aldehydes and ketones
prompt: Tollens' reagent oxidises CH₃CH=CHCHO (crotonaldehyde) to:
explain: Tollens' reagent is a mild oxidant: it oxidises –CHO to –COO⁻ and leaves C=C untouched.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: Mohr's salt solution + cold NaOH first gives a precipitate of which colour?
explain: Fe(OH)₂ is dirty green; on standing it oxidises in air to brown Fe(OH)₃.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Mohr's salt and potash alum
prompt: The pH of an aqueous solution of potash alum is:
options: Exactly 7, as it is a neutral salt
Less than 7, due to Al³⁺ hydrolysis
Greater than 7, due to K⁺ hydrolysis
Greater than 7, due to SO₄²⁻ hydrolysis
explain: Al³⁺ hydrolyses to give H⁺, so the solution is acidic. K⁺ and SO₄²⁻ do not hydrolyse appreciably.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: Coupling of benzenediazonium ion with aniline to give the azo dye is best carried out in which medium?
explain: Amine couplings need weakly acidic pH: strong acid protonates the amine, strong base destroys the diazonium ion.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of aniline yellow and iodoform
prompt: In the I₂/NaOH reaction of ethanol, which halogenated intermediate is cleaved by OH⁻ to give CHI₃?
explain: Ethanol is oxidised to CH₃CHO, tri-iodinated to CI₃CHO, then cleaved by OH⁻ to CHI₃ and formate.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: In the brown ring test, where does the brown ring appear after conc. H₂SO₄ is added along the tube wall?
options: At the junction of the two liquid layers
At the bottom of the test tube
At the top surface of the solution
explain: Dense conc. H₂SO₄ forms a lower layer; the complex forms where it meets the FeSO₄–nitrate layer.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Anion analysis: CO3, S, SO4, NO3, NO2 tests
prompt: Alkaline S²⁻ solution + sodium nitroprusside gives a complex of which colour?
explain: Sulphide forms the purple/violet complex Na₄[Fe(CN)₅NOS] with nitroprusside.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: Chromyl chloride test for Cl⁻: the solid chloride is heated with which pair of reagents?
explain: Solid chloride + K₂Cr₂O₇ + conc. H₂SO₄ on heating gives orange-red CrO₂Cl₂ vapours.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: AgCl dissolves in aqueous NH₃ because it forms which soluble species?
explain: Ag⁺ forms the linear diamminesilver(I) complex, lowering [Ag⁺] below Ksp of AgCl.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: A chloride heated with MnO₂ and conc. H₂SO₄ evolves which gas?
explain: MnO₂ oxidises HCl formed to greenish-yellow, pungent Cl₂ gas.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: Chloride + conc. H₂SO₄: gas evolved gives dense white fumes with a glass rod dipped in NH₃. The fumes are:
explain: Colourless pungent HCl gas combines with NH₃ to give white NH₄Cl fumes.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: Mohr's method of Cl⁻ titration with AgNO₃ must be done in which pH medium?
explain: In acid CrO₄²⁻ goes to Cr₂O₇²⁻; in strong base Ag₂O precipitates, so pH ≈ 6.5–10.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halide tests: Cl-, Br-, I-
prompt: On exposure to sunlight, white AgCl turns grey/purple due to formation of:
explain: AgCl is photosensitive; light decomposes it to finely divided silver.
